title: A locally separated group algebraic space over a field is a scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $G$ be a group algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: multiplication $G\times_kG\to G$, identity $\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ and inversion $G\to G$ are morphisms of algebraic spaces satisfying the group identities on every test scheme. Assume $G$ is locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], tested on etale scheme charts, and locally separated, meaning its diagonal is representable by immersions. Then $G$ is represented by a separated $k$-scheme locally of finite type, and its group operations are morphisms of that scheme, making it a group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Tag 08BH (lemma-group-scheme-over-field-separated), with the preceding paragraph explaining that locally separated spaces are decent; Tag 0B8F (lemma-group-space-scheme-locally-finite-type-over-k).

proof.text: The identity $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ is a rational section. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-separated-rational-point-closed-immersion] with $Z=G$ and the identity extension $K=k$. Its immersion-diagonal hypothesis is exactly local separatedness here. Thus $e$ is representable by closed immersions.

Put $d:G\times_kG\to G$, $d(g,h)=g^{-1}h$. For every test scheme, $d(g,h)=e$ if and only if $h=g$, so the square with top arrow $\Delta:G\to G\times_kG$, bottom arrow $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$, and right arrow $d$ is cartesian. To check the diagonal is a closed immersion, take any scheme $T\to G\times_kG$. Its pullback is $T\times_{G,d} \operatorname{Spec}k$. This is a scheme and a closed immersion into $T$ by the conclusion about $e$ in step 1. Equivalently, any further scheme pullback is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Thus $G/k$ is separated. This is the explicit cartesian-square argument of Tag 06P6, not an additional group-space representability theorem.

Choose an algebraic closure $\overline{k}$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-sfb-separated-group-space-geometric-scheme], the separated group space $G$ has $G_{\overline{k}}$ represented by a scheme $H$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] the base change is an algebraic space, and its pulled-back etale charts cover it. Base-changing multiplication, inverse and identity gives group operations on this sheaf. Applying [lem-pc-yoneda] with target functor $h_H$ and domains $H\times_{\overline{k}}H$, $H$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}$ gives unique scheme morphisms realizing them; injectivity of the same bijection gives their group identities. Choose a jointly surjective family of etale scheme charts $U_i\to G$, each $U_i$ locally of finite type over $k$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] the schemes $U_{i,\overline{k}}=U_i\times_G G_{\overline{k}}=U_i\times_k\overline{k}$ form a jointly surjective etale family over $G_{\overline{k}}\cong H$, and [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] makes each $U_{i,\overline{k}}$ locally of finite type over $\overline{k}$. Let $q:\coprod_iU_{i,\overline{k}}\to H$ be the induced map from the disjoint union. Each component is etale over $H$, hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; joint surjectivity on field-valued points gives surjectivity on points of $H$ (a point $x$ is the class of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to H$). The composite to $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}$ is locally of finite type componentwise. Hence [lem-a1-lft-flat-lfp-source-descent] shows that $H\to\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}$ is locally of finite type.

Apply [lem-sfb-group-finite-points-affine] to the group scheme $H/\overline{k}$ of step 3. It gives an affine open containing any prescribed finite list of $\overline{k}$-points, including the empty list. The hypotheses are local finite type and algebraic closedness; no quasi-compactness, smoothness or reducedness of $H$ has been used.

Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-affine-neighbourhood-scheme-descent] with $X=G$ and $Y=H$. The given local separatedness and local finite type give its hypotheses on $G$; step 3 gives its geometric representing scheme and step 4 gives its finite-point affine condition. Therefore $G$ is represented by a $k$-scheme $P$.

Use [lem-pc-yoneda] with domains $P\times_kP$, $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $P$ to turn the original multiplication, identity and inverse natural transformations into scheme morphisms. Their identities hold because Yoneda is injective and the original identities hold on all test schemes. Hence $P$ is a group scheme in [def-sc-group-scheme]. Under the representing isomorphism its diagonal is the diagonal proved closed in step 2, so $P/k$ is separated. Its structure morphism is locally of finite type: pulling the charts $U_i\to G$ of step 3 back along the representing isomorphism $P\cong G$ gives a jointly surjective family of etale scheme maps $U_i\to P$ with each $U_i$ locally of finite type over $k$, and the disjoint-union argument of step 3 with [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [lem-a1-lft-flat-lfp-source-descent] gives that $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. These are exactly the asserted properties.

lean.statement: theorem exists_groupScheme_of_locallySeparated {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (F : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{u}) (e : F ⋙ forget GrpCat ≅ G.obj.obj) (hlft : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ G.obj.obj), IsEtale a → LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 G.obj.obj) (𝟙 G.obj.obj))) : ∃ P : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))), IsSeparated P.X.hom ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType P.X.hom ∧ Nonempty (yonedaGrp.obj P ≅ F)
lean.note: The given group operations are encoded as a group-valued functor F with an isomorphism of its underlying presheaf to G. The representing group scheme P is required to have yonedaGrp.obj P isomorphic to that same F, retaining all operations. Local finite type is tested on every representable étale scheme chart; local separatedness uses scheme-test representability of the diagonal by immersions.
